faqDescription: Everything you want to know about Anacan, calculators, and daily use.
faq1Answer: Anacan is a daily assistant for menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and baby care. The app includes a calendar, notes, general AI information, community, and various tools.
faq2Answer: You can use the basic functions for free. Some additional functions require a Premium subscription. Prices and suitable offers are displayed by the App Store or Google Play before purchase.
faq3Answer: The website and app are available in Azerbaijani, English, Turkish, Russian, German, Arabic, Georgian, Kazakh, Uzbek, Chinese, Indonesian, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Vietnamese, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Dutch, and Swedish.
faq4Question: Does Dr. Anacan replace a doctor?
faq4Answer: No. Dr. Anacan is an AI assistant for general information and exploring questions. For diagnosis and treatment, speak with your doctor. In an emergency, contact your local emergency services.
faq5Question: Do I need an account to use the calculators?
faq5Answer: No. The ovulation and due date calculators on the website work for free and without registration. The dates you enter are calculated only in the browser and are not sent to the server.
faq6Question: How can my partner join me?
faq6Answer: The partner can create their own account and follow the invitation and joining steps in the app. This way, you can track the information you allow and your daily care together.
faq7Question: How do I manage my Premium subscription?
faq7Answer: Open the subscriptions section in your App Store or Google Play account. Deleting the app does not cancel the subscription. You can restore your existing purchase with the restore function in the app.
faq8Question: Where should I write for support?
faq8Answer: For general questions, write to info@anacan.az; for privacy issues, write to privacy@anacan.az. For technical problems, also include the app and device version.

ovulationIntro: Get to know your cycle's rhythm a little better. Enter the first day of your last menstruation and your usual cycle length.
cycleHelp: From the first day of one menstruation to the first day of the next. Usually 21–35 days; this tool accepts 21–45 days.
periodHelp: Number of days bleeding lasts. This does not change the ovulation date; it shows menstruation days on the calendar.
lutealHelp: From ovulation to the next menstruation. If you don't know, keep it at 14 days. The tool accepts 10–16 days.
dateError: Enter a valid date. The last menstruation date cannot be in the future.
cycleError: Cycle length must be 21–45, menstruation duration 1–10, and luteal phase 10–16 full days.
resultNote: These dates are estimates. Ovulation can vary each month; the calculator does not confirm pregnancy and is not used as a method of contraception.
ovulationGuideText: Ovulation is the release of an egg cell from the ovary. It usually occurs approximately 14 days before the next menstruation, but this period varies from person to person and from month to month.
fertileGuideText: The calculator adds the cycle length to the last menstrual period date and subtracts the duration of the luteal phase. The fertile window is the 5 days before ovulation and the day of ovulation. Considering that the egg can survive for approximately 12–24 hours, the next day is also shown on the calendar as an additional buffer day.
formula: Ovulation = Last Menstruation + Cycle Length − Luteal Phase
irregularGuideTitle: What if the cycle is irregular?
irregularGuideText: The average cycle length only provides an approximate plan. LH ovulation tests in urine and cervical mucus observations can provide additional information. Basal body temperature rise, however, usually indicates ovulation afterwards. If your cycle varies a lot, talk to your doctor.
ovulationFaq1Question: Does the calculator accurately show ovulation?
ovulationFaq1Answer: No. Calendar calculation does not measure ovulation; it is an estimate based on previous dates. Even regular cycles can have variations. For personal assessment, consult a doctor and use appropriate ovulation tests for accuracy.
ovulationFaq2Answer: Yes. Sperm can survive for several days in suitable conditions, and early ovulation is possible. The days shown on the calendar do not mean safe protection days.
ovulationFaq3Question: When should I take a pregnancy test?
ovulationFaq3Answer: Most home tests are more reliable from the first day of a missed period. If you don't know your next menstrual period date, test at least 21 days after unprotected intercourse. If the result is negative and the delay continues, repeat after a few days.
ovulationFaq4Question: Are the dates I entered saved?
ovulationFaq4Answer: The website calculator processes dates only on this browser page. It does not create an account or health record. When you export to a calendar, you choose where to save the file yourself.
dueDateTitle: Due date calculator — Calculate pregnancy week
dueDateIntro: Find out your estimated due date based on the first day of your last menstrual period. A small start to planning the stages of pregnancy.
dueDatePassed: Estimated date has passed. Clarify next steps with your doctor.
dueDateNote: The calculation is based on 280 days from the last menstrual period and the difference from a 28-day cycle. Ultrasound and doctor's assessment can clarify the date; this date is not a guarantee of birth.
dueDateError: Check the last menstrual period date. This tool accepts dates within the last 315 days.
dueDateGuideTitle: How is the due date calculated?
dueDateGuideText: The standard calculation adds 280 days to the first day of the last menstrual period. In regular cycles where the cycle is longer or shorter than 28 days, that difference is taken into account. In cases of irregular cycles, IVF, or unknown dates, the date given by the doctor may be more appropriate.
dueDateFaq1Question: Is pregnancy age calculated from the date of conception?
dueDateFaq1Answer: Usually, pregnancy age is calculated from the first day of the last menstrual period. Therefore, the calculated age is often approximately two weeks more than the time elapsed since conception.
dueDateFaq2Question: What if a different date is shown on the ultrasound?
dueDateFaq2Answer: Clarify with your doctor. Especially early ultrasound, when the last menstrual period date is unknown or in irregular cycles, can provide a more appropriate date.
symptomsTitle: Pregnancy symptoms — Early signs and trimester guide
symptomsIntro: Every pregnancy is different. Some changes are felt early, others later. Pregnancy cannot be diagnosed based on symptoms; a test and doctor's assessment are needed.
symptom1Text: If you have a regular cycle, a missed period can be an early sign of pregnancy. Stress, illness, and hormonal changes can also cause delays. Take the test according to its instructions; if the result is negative and the delay continues, repeat and talk to your doctor.
symptom2Text: Can occur at any time of day. Eating small, frequent meals, drinking water slowly, and avoiding smells that bother you can help. If you cannot keep down fluids, your urine output is reduced, or you feel very weak, seek medical attention.
symptom3Text: Hormonal changes can cause fullness and tenderness in the breasts. Comfortable, well-fitting clothing can help. Discuss any new lumps, one-sided redness, fever, or persistent pain with your doctor.
symptom4Text: It may be felt more in the first weeks and last trimester. Take time to rest, eat a balanced diet, and maintain appropriate light exercise. Severe fatigue, palpitations, or shortness of breath should be evaluated.
symptom5Text: Early hormonal changes and later pressure from the uterus can have an effect. Do not drastically reduce water intake for this. If there is burning, pain, bloody urine, or fever, consult a doctor.
symptom6Text: Cravings for certain foods or increased sensitivity to previously loved smells may occur. Maintain a balanced diet. If there is a craving for soil, paper, or other non-food items, talk to a doctor.
symptom7Text: Spotting in early pregnancy can have various causes; the cause cannot be known based on its appearance. If there is bleeding along with the possibility of pregnancy, contact a doctor. Heavy bleeding, one-sided pain, dizziness, or loss of consciousness should be evaluated urgently.
symptom8Text: Hormonal changes can slow bowel movements. Fibrous foods, sufficient water, and appropriate exercise can help. Talk to a doctor if there is severe pain, bloody stools, or persistent discomfort.
symptom9Text: Small portions, not lying down immediately after eating, and avoiding personal food triggers can help. Clarify medication choices with a doctor or pharmacist. Do not consider severe upper abdominal pain as ordinary reflux.
symptom10Text: Discomfort may arise as the body's weight and posture change. Talk to a doctor about comfortable support, appropriate light exercise, and physiotherapy if needed. Severe, sudden, or rhythmic pain should be evaluated.
symptom11Text: Movements often begin to be felt between weeks 16–24. Recognize your baby's usual movement pattern. If movements have decreased, stopped, or the usual pattern has changed, contact the maternity ward immediately; do not wait until the next day.
symptom12Text: Gradual leg swelling can occur in pregnancy. Rest and a comfortable position can help. Sudden swelling in the face and hands, headache, vision changes, or upper abdominal pain should be evaluated urgently.
symptom13Text: Braxton-Hicks contractions can be irregular and may decrease with a change in position. If contractions become regular, stronger, if water breaks, or if they start before week 37, talk to the maternity ward.
symptom14Text: Discomfort, frequent urination, and physical changes can disrupt sleep. A calm evening routine and a comfortable side position can help. Seek support for persistent insomnia or mood difficulties.
urgentTitle: When should you seek emergency help?
urgentText: Seek urgent medical evaluation if there is heavy bleeding, severe or one-sided abdominal pain, loss of consciousness, chest pain, severe shortness of breath, severe headache and vision changes, decreased baby movements, fluid leakage, or persistent vomiting. Contact local emergency services or the maternity ward.
symptomsFaq1Answer: Yes. The intensity and number of symptoms vary greatly. The absence of nausea and other symptoms alone does not indicate a problem. Confirm pregnancy with a test and medical evaluation.
symptomsFaq2Answer: Yes. Breast tenderness, fatigue, and mood changes can occur in both cases. Symptoms do not confirm pregnancy; it is more beneficial to test at the appropriate time.

simulatorIntro: Consider 5 daily situations with your partner. This test is not a medical evaluation; it's a conversation starter to share care together.
testEndText: Care is about listening and learning together, more than perfect answers. Share your daily plan in partner mode.
test1Question: The baby is ready for sleep. Which option is appropriate?
test1Option1: On their back, in an empty crib with a firm, flat mattress
test1Option2: On the sofa with a soft pillow and toy
test1Option3: On their side, with a thick blanket next to them
test1Explanation: For safe sleep, the baby sleeps on their back, on a firm, flat surface. The crib should not contain pillows, soft toys, or loose blankets.
test2Question: Your partner says they are very tired. What would you do?
test2Option1: Take on a specific task to help them rest
test2Option2: Tell them to endure a little longer
test2Option3: Wait until they ask for help themselves
test2Explanation: Listening and taking on specific responsibilities reduces the burden. For example, preparing food, changing diapers, or sharing household chores.
test3Question: How would you use the bottle when feeding the baby?
test3Option1: Hold the baby semi-upright in your arms with head and neck support
test3Option2: Prop the bottle with a pillow
test3Option3: Leave the baby alone, fully reclined
test3Explanation: When feeding, hold the baby in your arms, support their head and neck, and respond to their pauses. Do not prop the bottle with a support and leave the baby alone.
test4Question: The baby is crying and you feel very stressed. What would you do?
test4Option1: Place the baby safely in the crib, take a short break, and seek support
test4Option2: Shake them harder to try and make them stop crying
test4Explanation: Never shake a baby. If you are very stressed, place them in a safe place, take a short break, and ask for help from someone you trust. Contact a doctor for signs of illness.
test5Question: You are preparing for a doctor's appointment together. What helps?
test5Option1: Noting down questions and daily observations together
test5Option2: Making all decisions based only on the internet
test5Explanation: Daily notes and prepared questions make the conversation clearer. Online information does not replace a personalized doctor's assessment.
